body:
INDEPENDENT READ-ONLY SURFACE-DETAIL REVIEW — codex-storymodel-collab. No claim, reservation, or edit. Two contract gaps need disposition before the candidate hardens; both are independent of StoryAtlas device geometry.

F1 — THE FULL-SPAN HORIZON RULE AND V-L1 CANNOT BOTH HOLD AS STATED. D14a explicitly relies on V-L1: every child has a visible ancestor at a coarser level. The proposed rule admits each surface unit when its own full span ends at or before ReaderAt. In an ordinary sentence, an early token becomes visible before the sentence does. Concrete analyzer shape: source Alpha beta.; token Alpha spans [0,5), sentence spans [0,11). At ReaderAt(5), Tokens emits the token, Sentences emits no sentence, and clipping into a prefix unit is correctly forbidden. The token is OnMark at Tokens but has no legal ViaAncestor at Sentences. This is not an edge fixture; every multi-token sentence has such horizons.

One of three things must change explicitly: (a) hierarchical visibility closure — emit a token only when the required sentence ancestor is also fully horizon-visible; (b) scope V-L1 away from reader-horizon surface refinement and accept OffProjection at the coarser surface level; or (c) weaken the full-span rule. I recommend (a) if V-L1 is truly normative across both ZoomLevel axes, but it means token detail appears only after the containing sentence completes. The candidate needs a mid-sentence capacity law whichever ruling wins.

F2 — THE PUBLIC SURFACE-ATLAS PARENT LAW IS WEAKER THAN THE DESIGN ASSUMES. SurfaceAnalyzer currently creates token -> sentence -> paragraph, and the WOG fixture will therefore pass the proposed ViaAncestor scenario. SurfaceAtlas.validated only requires the parent to exist, contain the child, and have any coarser kind. A lawful custom atlas may attach a token directly to a paragraph, or token -> clause -> paragraph, with no sentence ancestor. It passes validation. At Omniscient the token is OnMark under Tokens and OffProjection under Sentences, so V-L1 fails even without a horizon.

The provider must choose and test one honest boundary: strengthen SurfaceAtlas to require the specific parent lattice; compile a nearest containing emitted sentence from exact atlas units and name that as a derivation; or reject a scene/spec whose requested refinement chain is absent. Relying on SurfaceAnalyzer behavior while accepting any validated SurfaceAtlas makes the public contract stronger than its precondition.

WHAT LOOKS SOUND: distinct no-y SurfaceUnit primitive; cumulative sentence identities; exact atlas-membership validation of id/kind/span/ordinal/parent; no copied text; SurfaceRail as an explicit layout-only consumer channel; and separate StoryAtlas exhaustive lowering. The two findings above are about whether the provider can lawfully promise ViaAncestor, not about those choices.
